elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New Section 16.7: "Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — "each Party" makes the cap bilateral, and no retained sentence states either Party's liability is unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 16.7: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Ono under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" — basis is "fees paid or payable" (not broader "all amounts"), lookback runs to the claim itself, and the USD 1,000,000 floor is present.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 16.5: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY ... BE LIABLE ... FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES SUFFERED BY THE OTHER PARTY" — already mutual and left unamended.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 Excluded Claims include "a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations", and Excluded Claims are expressly outside the cap ("Except for Excluded Claims").

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 Excluded Claims include "its data protection or security obligations".

16.7 Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2" — the same indemnities identified in retained 16.5, so the carve-out tracks every indemnity referenced in the liability article and is consistent (not contradictory) with 16.5.
16.7 Excluded Claims include "its gross negligence"; retained 16.5 likewise disapplies its limitation for gross negligence, so no conflict.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 Excluded Claims include "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 16.7: "Ono's payment obligations under this Agreement shall not constitute damages subject to this cap." Ono is the Licensee/Customer-side party under our aliases, and the exclusion covers payment obligations as a whole rather than a narrow defined subset, so the failing regex (which looks for the literal token "Customer") is a naming artefact only.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 16.7 uses "the fees paid or payable by Ono ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" as prong (a), with a USD 1,000,000 floor that only raises, never lowers, the cap.
Excluded Claims expressly include indemnification obligations under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly include breach of confidentiality obligations.
Excluded Claims expressly include gross negligence.
Excluded Claims expressly include willful misconduct.

reasons: Finding classification is sound: Article 16 as drafted contains only a mutual consequential-damages disclaimer (16.5) and no aggregate monetary cap, so the clause fails the fallback element requiring a mutual cap based on 12 months' fees; a redline is warranted.

The single inserted Section 16.7 is a concise insertion for a missing cap and carries no extras — no survival tail, no procedure, no added damages categories, no explanatory examples, and no deletion or paraphrase of retained language. Section 16.5 (including its favourable third-party-indemnity and gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-outs) is preserved verbatim, and the recall paragraph in the rendered block is untouched context.

Intent is preserved: 16.7's Excluded Claims list mirrors and does not contradict the carve-outs already stated in 16.5; there is no dangling cross-reference (Article 10, Sections 16.1 and 16.2 are the indemnities referenced by the existing text) and no term is left undefined by the edit.

The failing deterministic check on the payment carve-out is mechanical only: the operative sentence excludes "Ono's payment obligations under this Agreement" in full, and Ono is the Licensee/Customer-side party, so the element is met in substance. No repair needed.

Drafting caution (not a checklist failure): this pharma licence expresses consideration as upfront, milestone and royalty payments rather than "fees", so prong (a) risks being read as nil and the cap collapsing to the USD 1,000,000 floor. Rather than adding illustrative examples (which would break minimality), consider confirming with the business whether a floor at USD 1,000,000 is commercially adequate against Array given the deal size, since the cap is mutual and now limits Ono's recovery too.
